newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 222 bln levs Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit up to 222 bln levs Feb 28.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 24.3 billion levs in the second half of February to 222.1 billion levs, preliminary Finance Ministry figures showed.

"The increase was mainly a result of large interest payments on government securities and on direct loans from financial institutions," a Finance Ministry official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
The ministry paid a total of 62.995 billion levs interest on treasury paper and on loans from the Bulgarian National Bank, the State Savings Banks and commercial banks between February 18-28.
A percentage figure for the deficit was not available because no viable budget for 1997 was approved.

Bulgaria's parliament, which dissolved in February to clear the way for early elections in April, approved on January 31 a stop-gap budget bill to service large government debt payments and finance public spending until a viable budget is passed.
The deficit assumed in the stop-gap bill was limited to the amount of interest payments due on government debt.
The bill provided for a 100-percent increase in public employees' salaries, pensions and social benefits.

Under the bill, state debt would be refinanced through new government securities issues and a direct 20-year loan from the central bank. The amount of the credit was not specified. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
